name: What happens if the walls are not straight in a tub-to-shower conversion?

mainEntity.name: What happens when the old tub walls are out of square, bowed, or uneven during a shower conversion?
mainEntity.text: What happens when the old tub walls are out of square, bowed, or uneven during a shower conversion?

acceptedAnswer.text: Out-of-square walls are common in older homes, especially in the Los Angeles area. They can complicate panel installation, tile layout, door alignment, and waterproofing. A contractor may need to correct framing, add backer board, or adjust the shower enclosure so the finished system fits properly. If the problem is ignored, gaps, crooked lines, or leaking joints can appear after installation. This is why a thorough site measure matters before ordering glass or wall systems. Homeowners should ask whether the contractor expects wall correction work and whether it is included in the estimate. The issue is not just cosmetic; a shower enclosure must fit well enough to keep water inside and allow doors to operate correctly. The best remodel plans account for imperfect walls from the start instead of assuming the existing tub area is perfectly square.
acceptedAnswer.description: Uneven walls can affect how the new shower fits, how the glass is installed, and whether tile lines look straight. A contractor may need to shim, frame, or rebuild parts of the wall so the finished shower is watertight and visually aligned.
